newsitem.title: UK: W.Africa crude sales to Asia in lull after busy May.
newsitem.headline: W.Africa crude sales to Asia in lull after busy May.

text.p: Sales of West African crudes to Far East refiners have hit a lull with June buying getting off to a slow start after heavy May trade, dealers said on Tuesday.
Some traders said that while the arbitrage still looked wide open on paper, the fall-off in trade signalled a weaker market in June.
"We're in a protracted lull, June barrels are hardly moving although (sellers) are beginning to know the dates of their cargoes," said a trader for a European major.
The market for light Nigerian grades was particularly sluggish, traders said, but heavier grades from elsewhere in the region were starting to find homes in Asia.
At least two first decade June Angolan Cabindas and a few Gabonese Rabis had been sold, while a VLCC of half Cabinda and half Guinean Zafiro had been bought by a Chinese refiner, they said.
"The arb is still wide open and in theory the market still looks well supported, but I do worry about the fundamentals," said one trader active in the West African market.
Others expected trade to gather pace. "I think it'll take off soon. We're expecting quite a lot more to go to the other major markets like South Korea and Japan," a trader said.
Just a handful of May cargoes were still left unsold, with one trader offering a May 27-29 Qua Iboe at Dated Brent +45 cents.
All Nigerian Forcados cargoes loading up to May 21 would be delayed by two days after Shell Nigeria declared force majeure on exports last week, a trader for the major said.
